title: Put the brain on a schedule — automations that learn from every run
summary: An automation is a headless Claude run on a cadence you set: you describe the job in plain language, one dispatcher runs what is due, and the result lands as a dated document. Each one keeps a pattern it reads before every run and adds to after one, you can replay the session a run actually had, and the notification carries the result rather than announcing that a file was written.

title: Your agent, as an app — Chat is the screen every session opens in
summary: The in-app agent stops being a terminal: a native 12-state Chat screen where questions become clickable cards, tool calls become collapsible cards, and boards, images and video render in place. It is now the default screen for every Claude session, with the embedded TUI still one dropdown away as Terminal (legacy). What's New also became a release history — one page per version, built from real screenshots.

title: The brain starts forming opinions — falsifiable theses, re-tested every sleep cycle
summary: The proactive learning layer lands: claims your project makes about itself, with predictions registered before the evidence arrives, a cited evidence ledger, and a confidence derived by arithmetic rather than felt. Alongside it, funnel analytics in Lab — and What's New itself.

title: Every task gets its own Claude — and goal-skill takes the build the whole way
summary: Open a task and a dedicated Claude Code session is pinned inside the task view, maintaining the document rather than implementing it. The goal orchestrator was rewritten around it — builders fork and resume, judges stay clean — plus a live agent dock, sleep that stopped duplicating knowledge, and one-click delegation from the board.
